# SAG mills: to GMD or not to GMD 

SAG mills with Gearless Mill Drives (GMD) have marked the advent of large scale milling optimisation, but they have also presented a major source of potential risk to mine-plant throughput. For example, in 2008-2009, the Laguna Seca concentrator at Escondida, which processes between 35-40% of total milling ore production at Escondida, experienced problems result in a production loss of approximately 15% of copper concentrate for the 2008 financial year.  In an effort to shed some light on the risks associated with milling on a large scale, CRU focuses on SAG mills with GMDs in Chile, where several have failed in the past 10 years. The main findings are: 





- GMD failures vary from case to case, but three problems keep recurring: damage to the structural integrity of the GMD; instabilities in the magnetic nucleus of the stator of the GMD; and problems with insulation in the stator of the GMD. 

- Causes can be grouped in three main categories: dimensions; maintenance and operation; and altitude. 



- If SAG mills with GMDs shifted the techno-economic frontier upon their introduction, mine management has now come to find it safer to operate a fair distance from the frontier itself. 

The speed of GMD drives is variable, which allows different operating modes to be implemented, such as smooth starting and stopping.  As a result, it is possible to adapt the speed to suit the varying requirements of the material being ground.  As the drives have no need for a clutch or gearbox, there is less maintenance involved and downtimes are shorter.  Higher efficiency and lower energy consumption compared with conventional drives, reduces operating costs.

## **Pushing boundaries** 

GMD technology is more than four decades old.  The first GMD that was put into operation in 1969 at a cement mill in France and is still operating, having undergone some renovations along the way. Currently there are more than 100 GMDs in operation worldwide, powering mills in various industries, of which around 40% are Siemens design and 60% are ABB based.  A third company, General Electric, designed and installed one GMD unit, but abandoned its efforts soon after. 

In Chile, there are 26 GMD-based mills in operation.<sup>1</sup> Half power ball mills, while the other half power SAG mills.  The troublesome GMD-based mills have been those powering the large SAG mills, with a 

diameter of between 32-40 feet. Problems have also occurred outside Chile.  For example, in 1999-2000, and again in 2006, Newcrest’s Cadia copper-gold mine in Australia experienced structural instability and had to undergo significant repairs.  The industry learned from those experiences and implemented relevant design and operating guidances.  For instance, Los Pelambres and Candelaria GMDs were amended in-situ.

But what are the causes? Firstly, it is size related. SAG mills have grown considerably in both size and horsepower. SAG mills have often been running too long with too high charges, at too high temperatures and with too little monitoring and maintenance. In some cases, SAG mills have operated at temperatures above the design capacity, which may cause structural deformation (due to expanding metal) and corrosion and insulation 1 We have included Antamina, which is located in Peru, in this analysis increasing the total number of GMDs analysed to 30. © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 6 **December 2009** www.crumonitor.com issues in the stator cooling system (premature depletion but no change to maintenance intervals, also causing twisting of the magnetic core). Indeed, insufficient maintenance and high operating loads have often caused accelerated dust exposure of the equipment, and insulation to suffer premat

ure aging. Thirdly, altitude appears to have played a role, causing problems relating to insulation. ## **But things are looking brighter** Over the past two years, however, Siemens and ABB have implemented design changes so that mills are less likely to experience problems. We are also likely to see fewer problems in the future because mines have improved their GMD operating know-how. Firstly, the operators are running mills at reduce power. For example, during 2008, Escondida run its Laguna Seca mill on 15% less power. The Antamina SAG mill runs on 10% less power. Secondly, operators are becoming more aware of maintenance requirements, and as shown in the table on the right hand side, 2010 will see further maintenance and repairs. ### Maintenance and Repairs in 2010 at GMD based SAG mills |**Mine (Operator)**|**Repairs**| |---|---| |El Teniente (Codelco)|45 days downtime expected in January and February of 2010,
leading to 20-30% loss over the entire period.| |Collahuasi|Repairs are expected to the stator in 2010, leading to about 40
day downtime with a loss of 30-40% of production over the period.| |Escondida (BHP Billiton)|Committed to continuous monitoring and possible repairs
throughout 2010 but no specific downtime has been announced.| Data: CRU Analysis, ABB, Siemens CRU does not have access to sufficient data to carry out a global statistical review of GMD failures as opposed to other mill drive failures. This has been a decade of trial and error on part of operators and engineers, where all have learned and adapted. GMDs offer many benefits that traditional drives do not, and CRU suspects that Siemens and ABB will continue to promote GMDs and that the mining industry will continue to install them. # Copper production - In Chile, copper production increased 10% y-o-y in September according to Cochilco. This is the second increase after thirteen consecutive months of declines. Codelco produced 26,700t more mainly because of Codelco Norte (22,600t) as more concentrates been processed. In addition, Gaby produced 7,700t more as it has been reaching full production, which offset reductions at Andina and El Teniente. Collahuasi had a 38% y-o-y raise in September due a low comparative base (the debottlenecking project came on stream in Q4 2008). Escondida produced 4,900t more than in September 2008 due to the restart of its SAG mill at Laguna Seca concentrator. S pence showed a 5,600t increase in respect to September 2008 and we expect a considerable decline in October due to the workers’ strike. - In Peru, copper production decreased in September in 2% y-o-y. Antamina’s production declined by 14% (4,300t) to 26,600t; which was offset by y-o-y increases in production at Cerro Corona (2,500t more than in September 2008 as it reaches full capacity), Toquepala (2,500t) and Cerro Verde (3,500t).
